text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-proxy-high-tail-latency detected on prod-west (p99=6.4s, p95=1.9s) — elevated error rate for SSE/WebSocket clients. Triggered 3/4 runbooks.

alex (oncall): Paging. I'm on it, jumping into traces now. @jordan FYI you'll be my backup.

jordan (sre): Oncall sig received, pulling proxy metrics and recent deploys. Any customer reports yet?

sam (eng-runtime): I see a spike in outbound queue depth from the streaming runtime to the proxy around 14:02 UTC. Clients showing long flush times. Suspect client backpressure + proxy write buffers hitting kernel send buffer limits.

alex (oncall): Incident timeline: first anomaly 14:01:12 UTC, alerts fired 14:03:00. Current p50/p95/p99 from metrics: `0.11s / 1.9s / 6.4s`. Error rate + tail latency correlate with increased `socket_write_retries` on proxy.

nina (pm): Are any high-visibility customers impacted? Support, please triage.

lex (support): We have 4 open chats mentioning paused streams and repeated reconnects. Two customers reporting degraded UX in EU region; one flagged as high priority (acct-ACME).

maya (customer-success): Reached ACME, they confirm intermittent stalls and reconnects since ~14:00. They're on a demo call; asked for ETA.

jordan (sre): Quick mitigation plan: 1) increase proxy write timeout and kernel tcp_wmem tuning for contended hosts 2) enable graceful drop of oversized buffered clients to free headroom 3) route critical customers to backup pool in us-east while we stabilize. Thoughts?

sam (eng-runtime): Agrees. Also propose enabling short TTL prefix caching temporarily to reduce backend token gen pressure for long-lived streams. Will prepare a canary config.

alex (oncall): I'll apply the proxy timeout bump and socket keepalive adjustments on the affected hosts now. Doing a canary on 2/12 hosts first.

incident-bot: Action logged: `oncall:alex` executed `proxy-set write_timeout=15s keepalive=60` on hosts prod-west-{04,07}.

sam (eng-runtime): Observing drop in kernel `sendq` depth on canary host, p99 dropped to 3.1s after 90s. Good sign.

jordan (sre): Rolling to remaining hosts in waves of 3 with 60s observation windows. Also applying `net.core.wmem_max` bump from 212992 to 524288 on the proxy nodes as a temporary mitigation.

alex (oncall): Rolling complete. Post-roll metrics: p95 ~1.2s, p99 ~2.8s. Error rate trending down.

nina (pm): Good. Lex, please notify impacted customers with a short note: what's changed and expected ETA for full fix.

lex (support): Drafting message: "We applied targeted proxy config changes to reduce streaming stalls. You may see a brief reconnect; service should stabilize within ~15-30 minutes. Follow-up: durable fix in progress." Will send to ACME now.

maya (customer-success): ACME confirms streams resumed on demo, latency improved. They want root cause analysis timeline.

jordan (sre): Next steps for RCA: capture trace samples for the affected interval, inspect proxy connection churn and per-connection queue sizes, check for recent deploys to runtime/proxy between 13:45-14:05.

sam (eng-runtime): No runtime deploys in that window. But we did push a batching heuristic tweak yesterday which increases per-connection KV cache pressure for long sessions — instrumenting now to verify whether it amplified memory/queue usage under certain client patterns.

alex (oncall): Captured traces and tcp stats. Logs show a surge of slow consumers: many clients with persistently low read throughput causing backlog. Also saw several clients with repeated small writes leading to Nagle interactions; setting `TCP_NODELAY` on proxy upstream might help.

jordan (sre): Adding to mitigation checklist: 1) keep current proxy timeouts 2) enable `TCP_NODELAY` for streaming connections 3) introduce backpressure shed threshold so runtime can return 429 for clients that are persistently unread.

sam (eng-runtime): Working on quick runtime flag to shed slow-consumer connections. Can push a soft limit that returns a structured disconnect event so clients can backoff. Will test on staging then canary.

incident-bot: Page update — severity: SEV3 -> SEV2 (customer impact contained, partial service degradation).

alex (oncall): Documenting mitigation actions in incident tracker. Assigning postmortem owners: @jordan (RCA lead), @sam (runtime action), @nina (customer comms).

nina (pm): Timeline for full resolution? We need a short-term engineering fix (runtime shedding + proxy knobs) followed by a long-term: improved client-side backpressure guidance and better proxy buffering heuristics.

sam (eng-runtime): ETA for runtime soft-shed feature: 48h for a staged rollout and monitoring. Proxy tuning fine-grain improvements: 24h.

lex (support): Sent ACME an update, included temporary workaround (increase client read buffer/shorten keepalive) for their devs in case they still see issues.

maya (customer-success): ACME requests a postmortem and a follow-up call after RCA. Scheduling.

jordan (sre): Logging follow-up tasks: 
- collect and store `tcpdump` traces for 13:50-14:10 window (forensics)
- correlate per-connection application logs with proxy metrics via trace ids
- add alert refinement to avoid noisy low-level alerts next time (we want service-level SLO alerts, not raw queue growth).

alex (oncall): Handing off to night oncall in 2 hours. Leaving runbook notes and current metrics snapshot in the incident doc.

alex (oncall): @night-oncall (jules) — takeover note: keep an eye on p99 and error-rate, do not rollback proxy settings unless p99 increases >10% over baseline. If reoccur, escalate SEV1 and notify eng-runtime.

incident-bot: Incident annotated with tags: [streaming, sse, websocket, proxy, backpressure, p99, mitigation].

jordan (sre): Closing interim triage — system stabilized, customers notified. Will reopen if anomalies resurface. Full RCA work to follow.

nina (pm): Thanks team. Please add the customer impact blurb + timestamps to the postmortem draft.

lex (support): Marking thread as "oncall-handoff" in tracker and creating a follow-up support ticket for ACME.

sam (eng-runtime): Note for follow-up engineering: simulate high counts of slow-consumer clients in the chaos harness to reproduce and validate shedding behavior.

alex (oncall): Done for now. Leaving logs and graphs in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/4539990000 — will add raw traces once uploaded.

incident-bot: Incident archived to triage queue.

-- end of thread --
